proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains only a broad Licensee indemnity, and Article XIII expressly disclaims any Licensor liability for infringement claims. We have added the standard Licensor indemnity, including for IP infringement of the platform we license.

ops.text: Notwithstanding Article XIII or any other provision of this Agreement, Licensor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Licensee and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Licensed Technology, the Platform or any deliverable infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right; (b) Licensor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Licensee's data caused by Licensor; or (d) Licensor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Licensee shall give Licensor prompt notice of any such claim and reasonable cooperation, and Licensor shall control the defence and may not settle in a manner imposing obligations on Licensee without its consent.

proposal.summary: Add a Licensor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and wilful misconduct.

quote: ARTICLE XII INDEMNITY Licensee will be solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights granted by Licensor to Licensee under this Agreement, and Licensee shall defend, indemnify, and hold Licensor harmless
rationale: Indemnification runs one way only: we indemnify Licensor broadly for our exercise of the licence, the conduct of our business and any breach, while Licensor gives no indemnity at all and Article XIII expressly excludes any Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology. That is the walk-away case; we have inserted the standard Licensor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with usual procedure.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Licensor's ownership of its own platform is fine, but the Agreement is silent on our trade and client data and on customizations we pay for; we have confirmed we retain our data and receive a perpetual, royalty-free licence to paid-for deliverables.

ops.text: Licensee retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, content and materials provided by or generated by or on behalf of Licensee or its clients through the Platform, including all trade, order and client data ("Licensee Data"), and Licensor acquires no right in Licensee Data other than the limited right to process it to provide the Platform. Any customization, client front end or other deliverable developed for and paid for by Licensee is licensed to Licensee on a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free basis to use, modify and sublicense for its business purposes.

proposal.summary: Confirm Licensee ownership of its data and a perpetual licence to paid-for customizations.

quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
rationale: Licensor's ownership of its own platform is acceptable, but the Agreement says nothing about our trade, order and client data (which flows through the hosted Platform) and Article XXI only requires us to hand materials back to Licensor. Customization/front-end work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) falls into Licensor-owned Licensed Technology with no perpetual licence back and an express bar on modification — short of even the fallback. We have added a Licensee Data ownership sentence and a perpetual, royalty-free licence to paid-for deliverables.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The cap currently protects only Licensor and is set at one half of amounts paid, which is well below our floor; we have made it mutual at 12 months' fees and carved out confidentiality/data security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, which sit outside the cap.

ops.newText: (b) EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY LICENSEE TO LICENSOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. LICENSEE'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IS NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.
ops.oldText: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap mutual at 12 months' fees with standard uncapped carve-outs.

quote: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.
rationale: The cap is one-sided (Licensor only), set at one half of amounts paid — well below the 6-month floor — while our liability is expressly unlimited and we assume "all liabilities and risks" (p0029/p0037). There are no carve-outs for confidentiality, data security, indemnities or IP infringement; indeed Article XIII(a) disclaims Licensor liability for infringement claims entirely. Walk-away territory; we have made the cap mutual at 12 months' fees with standard uncapped Excluded Claims.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a blanket assignment bar with no affiliate/M&A carve-out, nor automatic termination of the licence on our change of control; we have added the carve-out and removed the change-of-control termination. We will also need to delete the Article XXII right of first refusal over a sale of our business.

ops.newText: Licensee may assign this Agreement and its license rights hereunder, without Licensor's consent, to an Affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, consolidation, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets; otherwise, Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
ops.oldText: Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.

ops.newText: (a) A Change of Control (as defined below) of Licensee shall not terminate this Agreement or any of Licensee's rights or licenses hereunder, and shall not give Licensor any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
ops.oldText: (a) Upon the occurrence of any Change of Control (as defined below) this Agreement and all Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder shall automatically terminate unless, prior to the occurrence of such Change of Control, Licensor has consented to such Change of Control in a writing executed by an officer of Licensor; provided that Licensor will not unreasonably withhold its consent to the consummation of a Change of Control.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out and delete change-of-control auto-termination.

quote: Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.
rationale: Assignment is blanket-prohibited for us with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, and Article XX provides that any Change of Control automatically terminates the Agreement and all our licences absent Licensor's consent — both walk-away items. Article XXII compounds this with a Licensor right of first refusal over a sale of our business. We have added the affiliate/successor carve-out and removed the change-of-control termination; the ROFR should also come out.

quote: Licensee acknowledges that the grant of the license set forth in this Section is a non-exclusive license and that the Licensor shall have the right to use and to license to other parties the Licensed Technology for any purpose and in any manner as Licensor may determine in its sole discretion.
rationale: The licence is expressly non-exclusive and there is no sole-supplier, requirements or "shall not procure from third parties" obligation on us; we remain free to source other FX platforms. The Article XXII "Right of First Refusal" is a ROFR over a sale of our business rather than a procurement exclusivity, and we have raised it under ASSIGN.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

quote: NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES
rationale: There are no liquidated damages, penalties or minimum-fee acceleration payable by us: Article XXIII expressly bars termination damages, and Licensor's retained right on early termination is limited to fees for trades actually performed. The audit cost-shifting on a 5% discrepancy is a customary reimbursement, not a penalty. Nothing to redline.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our licences must extend to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf; we have added them to the grant and to the corresponding access restriction, with a confidentiality condition.

ops.newText: grants to Licensee, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on Licensee's behalf, a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use
ops.oldText: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use

ops.newText: (e) disclose any Licensed Technology to, or permit the use or access of any Licensed Technology by any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on its behalf and bound by written confidentiality obligations, for use in the Field of Use.
ops.oldText: (e) disclose any Licensed Technology to, or permit the use or access of any Licensed Technology by any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee for use in the Field of Use.

proposal.summary: Extend the licence and permitted-access wording to Affiliates and contractors.

quote: (e) disclose any Licensed Technology to, or permit the use or access of any Licensed Technology by any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee for use in the Field of Use.
rationale: The grant runs to Licensee alone and access is expressly limited to our employees, with sublicensing, outsourcing and service-bureau use barred — Affiliates and contractors are excluded with no path to add them, which is the walk-away case. We have added Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (confidentiality-bound) to the grant and to the access restriction. We separately note the grant is conditioned on payment and terminable by Licensor on any breach, addressed under T4C.

quote: (a) use the Licensed Technology (all or any portion thereof) other than within the scope of the license granted by Licensor under this Agreement;
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds our business as such. Article II's restrictions and the "Field of Use" definition limit only how we may use Licensor's own technology (including a bar on Derivative Works of the Licensed Technology), which is ordinary licence scope, not a restraint on the products we may buy, build or sell. Nothing prevents us from using or developing alternative FX platforms.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A 36-month committed term with no exit right for us is not acceptable; we have added our standard 30 days' convenience termination with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. We can discuss 60 days' notice if that helps.

ops.text: IV Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, in which case Licensor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination and no early termination fee or other penalty shall be payable by Licensee.

proposal.summary: Add Licensee termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund.

quote: the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the "Initial Period"). The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor. Upon any breach by Licensee of any representation, warranty, covenant and/or obligation hereunder, the Licensor may immediately terminate this Agreement
rationale: We are locked into a 36-month term with no convenience termination right, which is the walk-away case for a multi-year term, while Licensor may terminate immediately on any breach by us (no materiality or cure period) and also on change of control or wind-up. We have inserted a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund and no penalty; 60 days' notice would be an acceptable fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Audits of our records must be limited in frequency; we have capped them at once per twelve months during business hours with a confidentiality undertaking and no access to our systems. The existing 5% cost-shifting threshold works for us.

ops.newText: Any such audit shall be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, during normal business hours, by an auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations, and shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor. No audit shall include access to Licensee's systems.
ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.

proposal.summary: Limit audits to once per 12 months, business hours, confidential auditor, no system access.

quote: Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement. Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
rationale: Audit frequency is unlimited — Licensor may demand audits at will — which fails even the fallback of once per year and sits in walk-away territory. The independent-auditor requirement, the 30-day lead time and the cost allocation (Licensor bears cost unless a 5% discrepancy, per p0064) are already at our preferred position; we have added the once-per-12-months, business-hours, confidentiality and no-system-access limits.

quote: shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, U.S.A., applicable to contracts entered in and performed entirely within the State of New York, U.S.A. without regard to any conflict of law principles.
rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the SDNY or the New York State courts in New York City matches our preferred position, and there is no arbitration provision. No change required.

quote: II. As compensation for the Licensee to use the Licensed Technology during the Initial Period, Licensee shall pay to Licensor, the following user fees:
rationale: The pricing schedule is a volume-tiered per-trade rate with a rebate mechanic in our favour; there is no most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation requiring us to extend Licensor the best terms we give any third party. Nothing to redline.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

quote: The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly.
rationale: Fees are purely usage-based per US$1m traded, with no minimum volume, take-or-pay or shortfall charge; the p0070 floor is simply a true-up to actual recorded volume. The fixed $2,500/month support fee and the 33% Supplemental Payments revenue share are separate commercial items, not volume commitments, and there are no caps on our usage.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A three-year, one-way non-solicit covering all Licensor and Affiliate personnel is outside our range; we have made it mutual, limited it to twelve months and to personnel actually involved in this engagement, keeping the existing general-advertising carve-out.

ops.newText: During the Term of this Agreement and during the twelve (12) month period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party who was directly involved in the performance of this Agreement to leave his or her employment with that party.
ops.oldText: During the Term of this Agreement and during the three year period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates to leave his or her employment with Licensor.

proposal.summary: Narrow the non-solicit to mutual, 12 months, personnel involved in the engagement.

quote: During the Term of this Agreement and during the three year period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates to leave his or her employment with Licensor.
rationale: The non-solicit binds only us, runs for three years post-termination (beyond the 24-month walk-away limit) and covers every employee of Licensor and its Affiliates rather than personnel involved in the engagement. The general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out is already acceptable; we have narrowed the clause to a mutual 12-month restriction limited to personnel directly involved.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A unilateral seven-year extension at Licensor's option is outside our range; renewals should be twelve months by mutual agreement with a capped uplift, consistent with the mutual-extension mechanic already in Article IV(II).

ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for additional periods of twelve (12) months by mutual written agreement of the parties, and any fee increase on renewal shall not exceed the lesser of CPI and three percent (3%).
ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.

proposal.summary: Replace the Licensor's unilateral 7-year renewal option with mutual 12-month renewals and a capped uplift.

quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
rationale: Renewal is a unilateral seven-year extension exercisable by Licensor alone, i.e. an automatic multi-year renewal with no opt-out for us — walk-away territory, and inconsistent with the mutual-extension mechanic in Article IV(II). We have replaced it with 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement and a capped uplift (lesser of CPI and 3%).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI requires us to return Licensor's materials within five days but says nothing about our own data or exit support; we have added transition assistance and a 30-day data return with certified deletion.

ops.text: In addition, upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (a) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return to Licensee all Licensee data, including trade, order and client records, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Add post-termination transition assistance and return of Licensee data.

quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control
rationale: Exit provisions run entirely against us: licences cut off immediately and we must return Licensor's materials within five days, with no transition assistance and no obligation on Licensor to return or export our trade, order and client data held on the hosted Platform. That is the walk-away case; we have inserted six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in machine-readable format within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter (90 days' assistance would be an acceptable fallback).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is currently fully \"AS IS\" with no conformance warranty or remedy, which we cannot accept for a hosted trading platform; we have added a 90-day conformance warranty, a workmanlike-services warranty and a repair/replace/refund remedy carved out of the disclaimer.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing disclaimer, Licensor warrants that (a) the Technical Support Services and any development or customization work will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following the acceptance date and following delivery of any Revision or deliverable, the Licensed Technology will conform in all material respects to the Documentation and Specifications; and (c) the Licensed Technology contains no viruses or other malicious code. Licensee's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Licensor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Licensed Technology or services. The disclaimer set out above does not apply to these express warranties.

proposal.summary: Insert an express performance/conformance warranty with a remedy, carved out of the disclaimer.

quote: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY
rationale: Article VIX is a pure "AS IS" disclaimer covering merchantability, non-infringement, fitness and title, and expressly denies any assurance that errors or non-conformity to Documentation will be corrected. There is no express performance or conformance warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy anywhere — only "commercially reasonable efforts" error correction (p0093) — which is the walk-away position. We have inserted a 90-day conformance warranty, a workmanlike-services warranty, a no-malicious-code warranty and the standard remedy, carved out of the disclaimer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance covenant even though Licensor hosts the platform and our trade data; we have added our standard coverages, and E&O of USD 1M plus cyber of USD 2M would be an acceptable fallback.

ops.text: (l) INSURANCE. Licensor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Licensor hosts or processes Licensee data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Licensor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a standard Licensor insurance covenant in the general provisions.

rationale: There is no insurance covenant anywhere in the Agreement (the only reference to insurance is as a cost we must bear under p0051), even though Licensor hosts the Platform and Hardware and processes our trade data. We have inserted our standard coverages (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M) with certificates on request; E&O 1M plus cyber 2M is our fallback.
